newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Peres chides Israeli right-wingers on peace process.
newsitem.headline: Peres chides Israeli right-wingers on peace process.

text.p: Former Prime Minister Shimon Peres lashed out on Wednesday against Israel's right wing for being unprepared to pay the price for peace with Palestinians.
"The right wing fancies that it can reach peace without paying for it," the Labour Party leader told journalists at the end of a three-day visit to Argentina.
Peres, 72, a Nobel Peace Prize winner and architect of peace accords with the PLO and Jordan, also criticised the government's policy of fostering Jewish settlements in Jerusalem's East sector.

Asked what he would do if he was in power, Peres answered: "I would try to avoid the building of settlements. We have the right to build them, but have no obligation to adopt measures that are not intelligent."
East Jerusalem was conquered in the Six-Day War of 1967 and later declared Israel's capital.
Peres also criticised a summit between U.S. President Bill Clinton and Netanyahu on Monday and Tuesday in Washington saying "That interview did not work out well. It was a bit disappointing."
"This kind of meeting has to be prepared beforehand, done with no improvisations," he added. The summit ended with no results to unlock a stalled peace process between Israel and the Palestinians.
Peres also spoke in favour of restarting stalled peace negotiations with Syria.
"The price of peace does not fall as time goes by, but delays do increase it."
In Argentina Peres received honorary doctorates and met the leaders of a country that is home to one of the world's largest Jewish communities.

Jews in Argentina have suffered two major attacks in recent years -- a bomb at the Israeli Embassy in 1992 that killed 29 people and one at the AMIA Jewish community centre in 1994 that killed 86. Those responsible for both attacks have not been caught.
